# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `gion help --reference`; don't edit by hand. -->

Every command takes `--md` for Markdown output meant for agents, and `-h` for its flags.

```text
usage: gion <command> [args]

commands:
  ls-refs <remote> [--prefix p]...     list remote refs (protocol v2)
  cat     <remote> <rev>:<path>        print a file's raw bytes
  ls      <remote> [<rev>[:<dir>]]     list a directory (default HEAD:)
  find    <remote> [<rev>] <pattern>  search file paths across the whole repo
                                       (substring, or glob with * ? ** [])
  grep    <remote> [<rev>] <regex> [--path p]... [-i] [-l] [--local|--forge]
          search file contents: scans locally when the candidate files are
          few (--max-files, default 5000), else asks GitHub code search for
          candidates and verifies them locally
  clone   <remote> <dir> [--ref r] [--path p]... [--no-git]
          light workspace: only the chosen paths (default all) at one
          commit, no history. it has a local .git that gion keeps in step,
          so pre-commit, git diff and git status work (--no-git: none).
          Then, inside it:
  status                               changed files vs. the clone
                                       (honors .gitignore)
  diff    [<path>...] [--stat|--name-only|--name-status]
                                       your edits as a unified diff
  log     [<path>]  /  blame <path>    history of the workspace's commit
  rebase  [<onto>]                     replay your branch onto <onto> (default:
                                       the default branch) and push it. on a
                                       conflict, fix the marked files, then
                                       rebase --continue | --skip | --abort
  add     <path>...                    widen the workspace with more paths
                                       (a new path just joins the scope)
  sync                                 pull upstream changes into files you
                                       haven't edited; stops on conflicts
  switch  <branch>                     move the workspace to an existing branch;
                                       keeps your edits, commits go there
  commit  -m <msg> [--branch b | --to b] [--no-verify]
                                       push workspace changes. default: first
                                       commit creates a branch, later ones
                                       update it. --to b pushes onto existing b.
                                       runs pre-commit and commit-msg
                                       hooks first
  commit  <remote> -m <msg> <path>=<local>... [--rm <path>]...
          [--branch <name> [--onto <rev> | --orphan] | --to <branch>]
          build a commit from the changes and push it; no checkout needed.
          each file's executable bit comes from the local file.
          default: new branch gion/<timestamp> from HEAD.
          --to: update an existing branch (compare-and-swap, retries on
          upstream moves that don't touch your paths).

  diff    <remote> [<rev>] [<rev>] [--path p]... [--stat|--name-only|--name-status] [-U n]
          what changed between two commits (a b or a..b), or what one commit
          changed (default HEAD). only the trees and files that differ are fetched
  log     <remote> [<rev>] [-n N] [--path p] [--oneline]
          commits newest first; --path: only those that changed it (GitHub
          answers that fast; elsewhere history is walked locally)
  blame   <remote> <rev>:<path> [-L a,b]
          which commit last changed each line (GitHub GraphQL, or locally)
  rebase  <remote> <branch> [--onto <rev>]
          the same without a workspace; stops (pushing nothing) on conflicts
  branch  rename <remote> <old> <new>
          rename a branch (GitHub keeps its open PRs). in a workspace:
          branch rename [<old>] <new>, <old> defaulting to the workspace's
          branch, which then follows the new name
  tag     <remote> <name> [<rev>] [-m <msg>]
          create a tag on the remote (annotated with -m); never moves one
  gc      [--max SIZE]                 trim the cache (~/.gion) now and show its
                                       size; it's also trimmed automatically
  skill   install [--project]          install the agent skill for Claude Code and
                                       agents reading .agents/skills (home dir,
                                       or the current project with --project)
  version                              print the gion version

<remote> is a URL or GitHub "owner/repo".
<rev> is a branch, tag, HEAD or commit id, with optional ~N / ^N steps
(main~2). Short commit ids work on GitHub.
flags: --md  markdown output for agents
`gion help --md` prints a usage guide for agents.
```

## `gion add`

```text
  --md                   markdown output
```

## `gion blame`

```text
  -L string              only lines a,b (1-based, inclusive)
  --local                compute locally even when the forge could answer
  --md                   markdown output
```

## `gion branch`

```text
  --md                   markdown output
```

## `gion cat`

```text
  (no flags)
```

## `gion clone`

```text
  --md                   markdown output
  --no-git               write no .git (by default gion keeps one in step for pre-commit, git diff and other git-based tools)
  --path value           path to include (repeatable; default whole repo)
  --ref string           rev to clone (default HEAD)
```

## `gion commit`

```text
  --branch string        new branch to create (default gion/<timestamp>)
  -m string              commit message (required)
  --md                   markdown output
  --no-verify            skip the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks
  --onto string          base rev for a new branch (default HEAD)
  --orphan               make a root commit with no parent (e.g. in an empty repo)
  --rm value             path to delete (repeatable)
  --to string            existing branch to update with compare-and-swap
```

## `gion diff`

```text
  -U int                 lines of context (default 3)
  --md                   markdown output
  --name-only            print only changed paths
  --name-status          print changed paths with A/M/D
  --path value           limit to this path (repeatable)
  --stat                 print lines added and removed per file
```

## `gion find`

```text
  --limit int            stop after this many results (0 = all)
  --md                   markdown output
```

## `gion gc`

```text
  --max string           size cap for this run (default $GION_CACHE_MAX or 1GB)
  --md                   markdown output
```

## `gion grep`

```text
  --forge                use the forge's code search to pick files
  -i                     case-insensitive
  -l                     print only names of files with matches
  --local                scan every candidate file, however many
  --max-files int        above this many candidates, use code search (default 5000)
  --md                   markdown output
  --path value           only files under this path or matching this glob (repeatable)
```

## `gion log`

```text
  --local                walk history locally even when the forge could answer
  --md                   markdown output
  -n int                 number of commits (default 20)
  --oneline              one line per commit
  --path string          only commits that changed this path
```

## `gion ls`

```text
  --md                   markdown output
```

## `gion ls-refs`

```text
  --prefix value         ref prefix to list (repeatable; default HEAD, refs/heads/)
  --time                 print elapsed time to stderr
```

## `gion rebase`

```text
  --abort                put everything back as before the rebase
  --continue             finish the stopped commit with your resolved files
  --md                   markdown output
  --onto string          remote mode: rev to rebase onto (default: the default branch)
  --skip                 drop the stopped commit
```

## `gion skill`

```text
  --md                   markdown output
  --project              install into the current directory instead of your home
```

  --md                   markdown output

  --md                   markdown output
